sections.eyebrow: Lead Experience Designer · End-to-End Journeys & Systems Design
sections.headline: Designing end-to-end journeys people can trust.
sections.lead: I work where product development and engineering meet, designing platforms that many teams and products depend on. I map the whole journey—every role and state, including paths needing feedback. From first contact to final action, my focus is turning complex processes into something people can actually use.
sections.tagline: End-to-End Flows · Journeys, Not Just Screens · Data-Driven

suggested.concept: Governed end-to-end journey motif: a horizontal flow of states in the brand maroon with an explicit recovery branch that rejoins the path — a literal rendering of 'every role and state, including paths needing feedback'. Built in code, no stock imagery.

alternates: Case-study cover collage strip (reuses existing assets, no new work)
Animated variant of the journey motif (CSS-only, respects prefers-reduced-motion)

subsections.headline: The journey behind the screens
subsections.subtitle: Here's what it actually takes to get there, and why it matters to the teams I work with.

cards.title: I map the full journey before I design a screen
bullets: Every step, handoff, and role mapped end-to-end
Recovery flows designed for when things go wrong
Fewer gaps discovered in QA, more time shipping

cards.title: I design AI into the journey, not on top of it
bullets: AI steps get evidence, designed states, and human review
Shipped in production across finance, telecom, and document intelligence
Trust built in at every step, not patched on after

cards.title: I follow the journey through to launch
bullets: Acceptance criteria and engineering feasibility reviewed together
Regressions caught in QA before they reach users
What ships matches what was designed

subsections.headline: Building the journey end-to-end
subsections.subtitle: The same five phases on every engagement, because connected, trustworthy journeys don't happen by accident. Select any phase to see what it looks like in practice.

subsections.headline: The whole system, not just the screen
subsections.quote: Good product design is what makes a system understandable: getting the flows right, designing the data well, and treating AI as core to the experience, not an afterthought.
